questions.stem: Recycling aluminium cans saves about 95% of the energy compared to extracting aluminium from bauxite ore. Why is the energy saving so dramatic for aluminium compared to other metals?

options.text: Aluminium cans are lighter than other metal cans
Extracting aluminium requires electrolysis, which uses enormous amounts of electricity; recycling only requires melting
Aluminium is the most abundant metal, so there is more to recycle
Other metals cannot be recycled

questions.explanation: Aluminium is extracted from bauxite ore by electrolysis of molten aluminium oxide, which requires huge amounts of electrical energy (about 15 kWh per kg). Recycling aluminium simply involves melting and recasting it (about 0.75 kWh per kg), saving approximately 95% of the energy. The metallic bonding in aluminium is maintained, so recycled aluminium has the same quality as new aluminium.

questions.stem: Plastic waste is a major environmental problem. Why is recycling mixed plastics more difficult than recycling glass or metal?

options.text: Plastics are too light to collect
Different types of plastic have different compositions and melting points, so they must be sorted before recycling; mixing them produces inferior products
Plastics cannot be melted
All plastics are biodegradable so recycling is unnecessary

questions.explanation: There are many different types of plastic (PET, HDPE, PVC, LDPE, PP, PS, etc.), each with different chemical compositions, melting points, and properties. If mixed together during recycling, the resulting product has poor and unpredictable properties. Sorting by type is essential but time-consuming and expensive. Glass and metal recycling is simpler because the materials are more uniform.

questions.stem: Some waste is disposed of by incineration (burning). What are the advantages and disadvantages of incineration compared to landfill?

options.text: Incineration produces no harmful emissions and is always preferred
Incineration reduces waste volume and can generate energy, but may release toxic gases if not properly controlled
Landfill is always better because it is natural
Incineration and landfill have identical environmental impacts

questions.explanation: Incineration reduces waste volume by up to 90% and the heat generated can produce electricity (energy from waste). However, burning plastics containing chlorine (like PVC) can release toxic hydrogen chloride and potentially dioxins if temperatures are not high enough. Modern incinerators have strict emission controls, but these add cost. Landfill avoids air pollution but risks soil and water contamination from leachate.

questions.stem: The 'waste hierarchy' prioritises approaches in this order: reduce, reuse, recycle, recover energy, dispose. Why is reducing waste considered the best option?

options.text: Because reducing is the cheapest option for businesses
Because reducing prevents waste from being created in the first place, avoiding all the environmental impacts of extraction, manufacture, transport, and disposal
Because recycling technology does not exist yet
Because all other methods are illegal

questions.explanation: Reducing waste at source means fewer raw materials are extracted, less energy is used in manufacturing, less transport is needed, and no disposal is required. Every other option in the hierarchy still requires energy and resources. For example, using a reusable water bottle eliminates the need to produce, transport, and dispose of hundreds of plastic bottles.

questions.stem: Glass can be recycled indefinitely without loss of quality, while paper can only be recycled about 5-7 times before the fibres become too short. What causes this difference?

options.text: Glass is more expensive than paper
Glass is an inorganic material that simply melts and reforms without degradation; paper fibres are organic polymers (cellulose) that shorten each time they are processed
Paper contains chemicals that prevent recycling
Glass is recycled at lower temperatures

questions.explanation: Glass is made of inorganic materials (mainly silicon dioxide) that melt and resolidify without any change in composition or quality — it can be recycled endlessly. Paper is made of cellulose fibres (natural polymers) that physically break and shorten during each recycling process (pulping, pressing, drying). After 5-7 cycles, the fibres are too short to hold together, so virgin fibres must be added.
